steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Is this everything, Ansel?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Yes. Reserve Op Team A4 is heading to Iron Fist City on a mission next month, so I don't need to trouble you to bring anything home for me.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: I know, but... don't you need to send some letters to your family?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: No... I'm alright.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Just take that letter to my friend. Ngala will figure it out for me.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Oh, right, only the big parcel is for him. This small box of antibiotics is for you. It'll be useful if you get bitten by a gloompincer out in the wilderness. Be sure to keep it on you.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Hah, if I run into your family, then I'll really be in trouble.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Alright, I'm off then, Ansel. Thanks a lot.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Right, I ought to get back to prepping myself.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Adnachiel
steps.text: Melantha, I can't see you from here. There's no way I can lay down covering fire!

steps.name: Adnachiel
steps.text: Two small gloompincers approaching from the northeast! Hold back, Cardigan!

steps.name: Adnachiel
steps.text: Keep to Ansel's medic support plan!

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: Don't worry, I won't let Ansel down!

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: Sniiiiff... Sniff... I smell it! It's a lure!

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: Melantha, the beast tamer controlling these gloompincers is definitely to the northeast. Might be hiding in the darkness of that mine entrance!

steps.name: Melantha
steps.text: Roger that. Steward... fall back, leave this to me.

steps.name: Melantha
steps.text: Can you take charge of escorting the target with Ansel?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Please lie down, ma'am.

steps.name: Panicked Merchant
steps.text: Lie down? Are you kidding me? Doctor, take us back to the vehicle!

steps.name: Panicked Merchant
steps.text: Did you not see the bugs and gloompincers? Did you not hear the bombs exploding?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Please, trust my teammates.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I'll be able to support them from this position, and they'll protect us better than the vehicle's sheet metal.

steps.name: Panicked Merchant
steps.text: A-Are you sure?

steps.name: Panicked Merchant
steps.text: Eeek!

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: The gloompincer that got you was venomous. I need you to remain calm and lie down to slow the bloodflow and get you treated. That's how we'll prevent permanent damage to your nervous system.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: But don't worry, I have an antidote with me.

steps.name: Panicked Merchant
steps.text: W-Well...

steps.name: Panicked Merchant
steps.text: Okay. I'll trust you, Doctor.

steps.name: Panicked Merchant
steps.text: Are you sure you've got the right antidote? What if you mistook the type of gloompincer? W-Will you compensate me?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I'm sure I didn't mistake anything. I'm very familiar with the beasts of Rim Billiton.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Alright, now please relax...

steps.name: Panicked Merchant
steps.text: Wait, D-Doctor, they're coming, over there—

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: Ansel, duck!

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: I dealt with the threats, and I've brought another casualty to safety!

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Very good, just give me a moment!

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Ma'am, your injection is done. You can rest for a while.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Now I need to treat the other injured on your team. Once all the treatment is finished, we'll proceed with the escort according to the mission briefing.

steps.name: Panicked Merchant
steps.text: *Pant* *pant*...

steps.name: Panicked Merchant
steps.text: Thank you...

steps.name: Panicked Merchant
steps.text: Doctor, has anyone ever told you that, at your age, as calm as you are, you're a little... intimidating?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: No, I'm just very focused on doing what I need to do.

steps.name: Panicked Merchant
steps.text: But you really are impressive. You must've saved a lot of lives.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: Ansel, what's your status?

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: Why'd you turn all gloomy?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: The nutritional supplements are in the bag. I'll get to your wound straight away.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Sorry, I was just distracted for a moment.

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: Hah, it just goes to show that your teammates are trustworthy.

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: I'm fine, just a scratch.

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: But you... have you found some time to recharge a bit?

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: *Sigh*... Ever since you came back to Rim Billiton, you've been working like this, day and night. You're forgetting to take care of yourself.

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: Surely you've had several operators coming to pick up those night shifts?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I'm just used to the rhythm of night work.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I'm just...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I'm just thinking, do I deserve the appreciation I get? As a doctor?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Do you think I've saved enough lives?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: The physical results are in, Melantha, nothing to worry about. Everyone's in good shape, no injuries sustained during the mission, and no worsened infections.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I'll tell the others in the morning... huh?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Why are you all still awake? Get to bed!

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Especially you, Cardigan. Don't forget we're going to the Originium processing plant tomorrow! We can't have you falling asleep in the meeting again!

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: But we're not done tasting all these weird Rim Billitonian snacks!

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: Sugar papaya leaf rolls, fried dandelion fowlbeast egg...

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: Who wants to try this next one? Hibiscus warned us away from it, saying it's bad for your blood sugar. And Ansel says not to eat it, but he's always stocking up on the stuff. Any takers?

steps.name: Adnachiel
steps.text: After that description, who would say no?

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: Hah!

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: —Here, Iron Fist City artisanal peppermint candy. Take a piece.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Thanks...

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: It's tough, what you said today, that thought weighing on your mind.

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: If I were you, I would definitely hesitate before walking into that house.

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: 'If you don't take my place, can I really call you my successor?' That uncle of yours is real tough. Not easy to answer at all.

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: —But you can't let it get to you, you still have to take care of yourself.

steps.name: Adnachiel
steps.text: Yeah. Even if you prove yourself a great doctor to your uncle, how are the rest of us supposed to buy it when you tell us to take care of ourselves?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Alright... I'll finish my midnight snack and then get some rest! Really! No more passing out on the stairs!

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: Melantha, do you think we can believe Ansel this time?

steps.name: Melantha
steps.text: Hm... maybe just this once.

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: Alright then, Ansel, we'll go on ahead! Call me if you fall down the stairs, I'll catch you before you hit the bottom!

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: Does Ansel still think we don't know Cautuses aren't a naturally nocturnal race?

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: Alright, nothing wrong with him sneaking in some late night snacks. It'll help him hold up through PT...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: —Hello, you've reached the Rhodes Island branch office in Iron Fist City, Rim Billiton.

steps.name: Passionate Male Voice
steps.text: G'day, I'm looking for...

steps.name: Passionate Male Voice
steps.text: Wait a minute, Ansel? You're the one answering the phone, right? I knew it was you as soon as I heard your voice! You're here!

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: —Ngala?!

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: How long has it been since I last heard your voice?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I thought you would've sent word by Messenger telling me when you had time.

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: Hah, I saw your company's number in the Yellow Pages, so I went for a phone booth.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: The one by your house with all the cartoon stickers? Or the one near the refinery that got burned?

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: Yeah, nah, the roads here have all been redone. Don't worry, I'll show you around in a few days.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: How did you know I'm just about to rush out the door?

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: You think I don't know you?

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: Aw, hearing you in such good spirits puts my heart at ease. Sounds like that company is treating you right.

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: You remember when you were interning two years ago? We couldn't find anything about your company.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Yeah, I was worried too. The Yellow Pages even had the address and number for the grocer downstairs, so I thought maybe the company was a scam.

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: Ever since you learned that canned spinach doesn't actually make you stronger, you've been slow to trust.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Ugh, let's not talk about that... I was so let down, after all those hopeful years scarfing down spinach.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: You know, when I was a kid, I really wanted to get into some kind of athletics. Football or factory parkour or something.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: How many times did I say it? I wanted to be like you, tall and strong from a young age, putting in all that work for the family without getting tired.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: But all I could manage was running with the boys for a few minutes before I got winded and dizzy and ended up watching from the sidelines.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: If you hadn't suggested giving me a megaphone to do commentary, I would've probably been standing there alone all that time.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: That time we all decided to sneak out at night to hit the slag field and watch our neighborhood team do the tug-of-war with the boys across the way...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: The floodlights on the slag field were glaringly bright. Everybody was cheering, and I had my little notebook, diligently jotting down all the slogans and comments I thought could be cool.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: It all seems ridiculous now, of course.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Hah, sorry, I ended up going into all that on our call here...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Ngala...? Are you still there?

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: Oh... Uh, yeah. No worries.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Do you... feel sick at all? Any discomfort?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Have you been taking the medicine I sent you? Remember the self-assessment criteria for Oripathy I mentioned a few times before?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: When do you think you might be free? If you can't go to a hospital for a proper exam, I could at least do a basic checkup...

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: Pfft! Hahaha! Settle down, Ansel.

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: How's your own health, by the way? You had, what was it...? Anemia?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Oh, me? I'm fine, nothing to worry about at all. I may have been diagnosed with an incurable congenital disease, but I'm only exhibiting mild symptoms...

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: But, Doctor, that's not how you put it when you found out I had Oripathy.

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: You said something like 'current methods can't cure it,' I think?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Yes, you're right.

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: I know you want to save more lives with your skills and prove to your uncle that what you're doing is meaningful.

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: But didn't you start studying medicine to save yourself?

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: Don't let it get to you.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: ...Maybe I am a bit too eager now that I'm back home. I've got this idea that everything I'm doing has to do with my family and friends here.

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: Sure, just don't worry so much. Do as you always did, focus on what you can actually accomplish, and leave the rest to your chums.

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: Let's meet up tomorrow night. The usual place. We'll have a late snack.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I don't know... are you sure?

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: Sorry, Rhodes Islanders, I'm still finding it hard to see the value in the Oripathy suppressants you're proposing.

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: And, as you can see, we have new protective equipment for the workers and two new assembly lines. We have no plans to upgrade equipment or increase Oripathy protection measures.

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: Your proposal is just too expensive. And it comes with too much we don't need.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Please wait, ma'am...!

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: We've been over this a dozen times now, Doctor.

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: Let's leave it here for today.

steps.name: Melantha
steps.text: She's wrong, Ansel. They don't have reliable channels for the workers to buy their medicine.

steps.name: Melantha
steps.text: But... you gave such a detailed and professional explanation. Why couldn't you convince them?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: It was always going to end like that.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: In Rim Billiton, people tend to trust the experience of their forebears and the word of mouth from their neighbors.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Especially when it comes to medicine, things are rough for Rim Billitonians, but the medical sector is pretty underdeveloped here.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: So you get people saying things are less serious than they are, mistakenly telling each other they don't need a doctor...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Everyone wants to solve their minor issues at home. So you get quack miracle cures suddenly becoming popular in this neighborhood or that.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I was prepared for this from the beginning.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: But I still feel... a little disappointed.

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: Oh, but you were so excited when you heard this company was interested in collaborating.

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: You prepared so much. You even tried to work with a third-party logistics provider to reduce costs.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Yes, though I had some selfish motives here...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: A big Rim Billitonian company like this will have tens of thousands of workers. I can't help but think some of the workers who get this Oripathy protection could be my friends and relatives.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I really wanted to prove that becoming a doctor meant something, was worth something, that I could do something for them.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: It's really disappointing.

steps.name: Melantha
steps.text: Don't worry, Ansel... This day is done, but tomorrow is a new day.

steps.name: Melantha
steps.text: You can try again, like you always do.

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: Yeah! If you believe you're right, just stick with it until you convince them, right? I kind of thought you'd chase her down and keep going, actually.

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: Besides, you said it yourself, Ansel, you want to save more lives. You can't call that selfish.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I just...

steps.name: Solemn Man
steps.text: Ansel. Can you make sense of Uncle Donnie's report?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Hm... There are abnormal shadows in his organs, taken together with his lung issues, these imaging tests show...

steps.name: Solemn Man
steps.text: In a word, it's Oripathy, right?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Yes, Uncle.

steps.name: Solemn Man
steps.text: Is there anything you can do?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I told him to quit working in the mines, but...

steps.name: Solemn Man
steps.text: Not everyone has the same options you do.

steps.name: Solemn Man
steps.text: I hope you make the right choice. Choose to do what you need to do.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Maybe I just know the place too well, so no matter how hard I try, I can't do anything.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Sorry, it's time for me to meet an old high school chum. You all head back to the office.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Huh, it's just like Ngala said, even the old phone booth here got renovated... Hah, is it supposed to be carrot colored now?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: The grocer's little window still has that black oil smudge.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Hm, I wonder if Ngala likes soda? I'll buy him a bottle...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: ...If you need medicine, you'll turn to the black market when you get desperate, right?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I'm sorry, please hear me out.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Sir, do you need Oripathy medicine?

steps.name: Infected Worker
steps.text: Um, well, yes... my partner really needs it.

steps.name: Infected Worker
steps.text: He's right over there, but he can't stand...
Ansel looks and spies a familiar figure.

a.text: Hey! Melantha! Cardigan! Are you in?! I'm taking my friend in to the office for a checkup!

steps.text: Shhh... It's okay, Ansel, it just hurt for a little bit. That worker made a big fuss over nothing.
Don't worry about me, it's not worth your time. We haven't met in ages, and you still have to tell me about all the places you've been.

a.text: What happened to the medicine I sent you? Do you know how bad you look right now?
You haven't been Infected for long. Why are you deteriorating so quickly? You're a mine engineer, don't you have protective gear?

steps.text: Relax, you only go to the doctor for serious stuff, right? I'm fine. It doesn't hurt that bad.
There's a lot of workers out there sicker than me. With wives and kids too... I pass the medicine off to them.

a.text: No, Ngala, how many times have I told you, you can't...
Pain is the body's warning system, not a normal thing you're supposed to bear with. And doctors aren't just for serious illness...

steps.text: Oh come on, your company's medicine really works, I've heard all sorts of great things about it. Ansel, you really can be proud of what you're doing. I know I am!

a.text: How is it that I really can't do anything?

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: Was that man just now... Ansel's friend?

steps.name: Cardigan
steps.text: He's in bad shape... Under his jacket, he's got lots of exposed Originium crystals on his arms and chest.

steps.name: Adnachiel
steps.text: But he's pretty lucid. Meaning it's not an acute infection, he's developed that over time.

steps.name: Adnachiel
steps.text: *sigh*... I think I get why Ansel wanted to be a doctor so badly, and why is family was so reluctant.

steps.name: Melantha
steps.text: Ansel...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: ...I've got the test results.

steps.name: Adnachiel
steps.text: It's hard to say right to the guy's face. We could help you talk your way out of it, if you want.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: No need... I already told him.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: He's been mentally prepared for it for a long time. In a mining district like this, Infected keep on working together. I'm sure he's seen... lots of similar cases.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: He's just too used to it all.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: If only I'd come back a bit earlier... if only I'd been harsher when telling him to assess his condition and take his medication...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: If only I had realized that pain perception varies from person to person, if only I could've changed the mindset that doctors are only for serious illness...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: If only medical standards in Rim Billiton were higher, and if only awareness of Oripathy protection measures was more widespread...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: His condition has progressed from mid- to late-stage now. At this point, any suppression methods I know are no longer effective.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: He might have two years, or one... I couldn't put it off any longer.

steps.name: Melantha
steps.text: I'm sorry, Ansel... I wish I could help you, or comfort you, but...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: No, it's alright. I'm the one who's sorry.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I shouldn't have told you all this...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: ...I'm the sickly one who always needed help, why is it someone else who gets struck down by illness first?

steps.name: Ngala
steps.text: Don't pull me, Ansel, I'm worried you could pass out on the street at any moment.

steps.name: Adnachiel
steps.text: Yeah, I'm a better shot with my crossbow now, seeing as I'm stronger and all. Meaning I can support you from a greater distance.

steps.name: Steward
steps.text: I can grasp the tail of those Arts... Don't worry, Ansel, my infection hasn't worsened. I just feel like I'm understanding it better.

steps.name: Melantha
steps.text: No problem, I'll... move to strike alone. Thanks to Franka's instruction, my swordplay is tougher, and I won't get knocked down so easily.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Yes, Ansel. Rhodes Island's Oripathy research is rather advanced.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: But for now, our conclusion is that we can't reverse the progression of the disease. We can only buy some time for our patients, stolen from the hands of death.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Of course, if you aspire to be a surgeon, you may have less direct contact with Oripathy.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: But, since you're a doctor, what we do is more or less the same.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: We look death in the eye and say: 'Not today.' Over and over again.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: ...I... didn't have a choice in the first place.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I'll never accept that there are things I can't do or lives I can't save.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: 'Just not today.'

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: That's all I can say... as a doctor.
